title: predict
summary: Predict responses from a fitted model.

gpu_support.notes: Supported deep-learning network routes execute on resident GPU inputs without gathering; unsupported explicit gpuArray routes return an error. Implemented statistical predictors gather to host.

description: `predict(mdl,Xnew)` evaluates supported fitted model objects, including `LinearModel` from `fitlm`, `ClassificationTree` from `fitctree`, and supported Deep Learning network objects, on new predictor data.
behaviors: Typed-integer predictors and numeric controls for implemented statistical models are independently gated RunMat-mode extensions with checked double boundaries; supported deep-learning models retain their documented integer-input contract.
`Xnew` can be a numeric matrix with the same predictor column count used during fitting.
For table input, predictor variables are selected by the model's `PredictorNames` property.
For `LinearModel`, `[ypred,yci] = predict(...)` returns pointwise confidence intervals for curve predictions by default.
For `ClassificationTree`, `[label,score,node,cnum] = predict(...)` returns predicted class labels, posterior probabilities, one-based leaf node ids, and one-based class-number predictions.

Deep-learning network prediction uses the same admitted sequential layer execution as `forward`. A formatted dlarray input returns a formatted dlarray in the network output axis order; an unformatted dlarray input returns an unformatted dlarray. Raw numeric input returns a numeric score array.

For an unformatted dlarray, an output with the same rank retains the input axis order; when the rank changes, batch precedes the remaining output axes. Raw numeric predictions retain RunMat's observation-major presentation.

Deep-learning prediction accepts `ObservationsIn` with `rows` or `columns`. A formatted dlarray with incompatible labels is rejected rather than relabeled; the original dlarray and its differentiation provenance are preserved.
A dlnetwork can return updated State as the second output. The current SeriesNetwork and DAGNetwork compatibility routes return one output.

Linear-model name-value options `Alpha`, `Prediction`, and `Simultaneous` are accepted. `Prediction` can be `curve` or `observation`; `Simultaneous` must be false because simultaneous intervals are not supported yet.
Classification-tree prediction currently accepts matrix or table predictor data and raises explicit errors for unsupported pruning/subtree options.

examples.output: yci is a two-column matrix with lower and upper bounds.

examples.description: Predict classes from a classification tree
examples.output: label is [0; 1], and score has one posterior-probability column per class.
scores has one row per observation.

faqs.question: Which model classes are supported?
faqs.answer: Currently `predict` supports `LinearModel` objects returned by `fitlm`, `ClassificationTree` objects returned by `fitctree`, and supported Deep Learning network compatibility objects.
